item.title: Sunil Mittal responds to Musk, says Eutelsat OneWeb also awaiting approvals
item.description: The Bharti Enterprises chairman said satellite services could begin 'hopefully soon' and also backed a common global framework to deepen telecom manufacturing ...
item.dc:creator: Gulveen Aulakh
item.content:encoded: Satellite communications company Eutelsat OneWeb is awaiting approvals from the central government, said Sunil Mittal, chairman of Bharti Enterprises, the largest shareholder in the Eutelsat group, the merged entity of French satellite major Eutelsat and the UK’s OneWeb, backed by the Bharti group. Mittal’s comments came in response to questions from the media about allegations made by American billionaire Elon Musk, founder of SpaceX and its satellite broadband service Starlink, that Starlink’s entry into India was being blocked by “certain oligarchs”. “We’re waiting for our own approvals,” Mittal said on Thursday on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress. He added that the group’s satellite services would begin “hopefully soon” in India. Musk’s comments, made late Wednesday on the social media platform X, which he also owns, triggered a debate online, with some arguing that satellite broadband services would cater only to the remotest regions of the country, which account for a very small percentage of India’s geography, while the majority of regions are already covered by terrestrial networks. Asked about the upcoming initial public offering (IPO) of rival Reliance Jio, the country’s largest telecommunications (telecom) services provider, Mittal said the industry was awaiting the public listing. “We’re all looking forward to a huge, successful IPO,” he said. On concerns that telecom manufacturing was not growing at scale in India, Mittal said an international framework was required to advance the segment. “The message is very clear. I was a part of the GSMA (Global System for Mobile Communications Association) delegation. We spoke at length and looked to the whole world to create an international framework on the lines of what the aviation industry has — common standards, common technologies. That is a very good way of moving forward,” he said. He added that as technology develops, more domestic manufacturing players could become part of the ecosystem of network providers that Bharti Airtel may add to its networks.

item.title: PepsiCo cuts forecast, deepens cost cuts as North America recovery lags
item.description: PepsiCo cuts its 2026 core earnings forecast and plans deeper cost reductions as weak North American demand and margin pressure delay its turnaround.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / PepsiCo cuts forecast, deepens cost cuts as North America recovery lags

PepsiCo cuts forecast, deepens cost cuts as North America recovery lags PepsiCo cuts its 2026 core earnings forecast and plans deeper cost reductions as weak North American demand and margin pressure delay its turnaround.

PepsiCo's third-quarter revenue exceeded market expectations and the company adjusted its 2026 organic revenue forecast to about 3% from a prior view of 2% to 4%, but flagged slow progress and profitability struggles in North America

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 08 2026 | 7:49 PM IST

Listen to This Article

PepsiCo warned on Thursday that growth and margin recovery in its key North American market was taking longer than planned and said it would pursue additional cost cuts to offset sluggish demand for its snacks and beverages.   Faced with high input costs, inflation-hit demand and the growing threat of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, the company is pursuing record productivity savings in its turnaround efforts launched after activist investor Elliott Investment Management took a roughly $4 billion stake a year ago.   PepsiCo's third-quarter revenue exceeded market expectations and the company adjusted its 2026 organic revenue forecast to about 3% from a prior view of 2% to 4%, but flagged slow progress and profitability struggles in North America.

"In North America, we remain committed to improving growth and core operating margin," said CFO Steve Schmitt in prepared remarks. "However, it is taking more time than we planned.   "Therefore, we expect North America's core operating margin performance to remain under pressure in the fourth quarter." Also Read

At UNGA, Trump vows 'unmatched military might' against drug cartels

Sustainability programme drives growth, India key to expansion: PepsiCo

PepsiCo is bullish on India, targets top-10 global market status

PepsiCo India opens fifth food plant in Assam with ₹778 crore investment

6 months of West Asia war: Market winners, losers & the road ahead

PepsiCo's core operating margin dropped 35 basis points in the third quarter from a year ago and was down 25 basis points year to date at 16.5% of revenue. In December, after discussions with Elliott, PepsiCo said it was targeting a 100-basis-point uptick over three years.   The company also cut its fiscal 2026 forecast for core earnings per share after adjusting for currency fluctuations to an increase of 1% to 2%, compared with previous expectations for the low end of the 4% to 6% range.

The challenge is industry-wide. Packaged food makers such as General Mills, McCormick and Conagra Brands are spending more on promotions and affordability initiatives to revive demand while contending with higher input costs.   PepsiCo, whose shares were up about 1% in early trading, is expanding its range of high-protein products to tackle the GLP-1 threat and is now promising extra productivity savings.   "Additional structural cost reduction actions are being identified and will be implemented in the coming months to help fund investments that aim to accelerate organic revenue growth and mitigate the impacts of rising input cost inflation," CEO Ramon Laguarta said in a statement.

PepsiCo's international business continues to perform well, but North America weakness, where third-quarter volumes in food were flat and dipped 2% in beverages from a year ago, is a persistent pain point.   "The beverage business continues to disappoint, and we expect PepsiCo will continue to be a source of share to both Coca-Cola and Keurig Dr Pepper," said Nik Modi, analyst at RBC Capital Markets. "PepsiCo will have to fully refranchise its beverage business or it will continue to lose share."   The company cut prices by up to 15% on products such as Lay's and Doritos in February, but last month said it would raise some chip prices to keep pace with input cost inflation.

CEO Laguarta has bought some goodwill with the international numbers, but the pressure he is under is high and rising, said David Wagner, head of equity and portfolio manager at PepsiCo investor Aptus Capital Advisors, noting that patience from the board and activists is finite.   "Next couple of quarters need to show real North American inflection, or the pressure moves from 'deliver the turnaround' to 'explain why you're still the right person to lead it'," he said.   More From This Section

item.title: Samsung sees record $80 bn quarterly profit as AI chip demand surges
item.description: Samsung forecasts record Q3 profit of 107.4 trillion won as AI-driven memory chip demand fuels earnings, while tight supply and rising chip costs pressure its smartphone business.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Samsung sees record $80 bn quarterly profit as AI chip demand surges

Samsung sees record $80 bn quarterly profit as AI chip demand surges Samsung forecasts record Q3 profit of 107.4 trillion won as AI-driven memory chip demand fuels earnings, while tight supply and rising chip costs pressure its smartphone business.

The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion) for the July-September period | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 08 2026 | 7:13 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected its quarterly profit would top 100 trillion won, a world first for a technology company, estimating a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter earnings as booming demand for AI chips drove strong memory sales.   The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion) for the July-September period, slightly ahead of an LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won.   The forecast marks Samsung's fourth straight quarter of record operating profit, underscoring a deepening global memory chip shortage as AI infrastructure investment outpaces supply growth, which has driven chip prices up sharply.   Samsung and Micron expect the imbalance to persist into 2028, although Chinese competition and a potential slowdown in AI spending pose risks to the longer-term earnings outlook.

Samsung's shares moved sideways despite flagging another record profit, slipping 0.2% in early trade versus a 0.5% fall in the benchmark KOSPI. Its share price has slumped more than 25% from a record high in June amid concerns about the durability of the AI boom. Also Read

6G, AI-native networks take centre stage at India Mobile Congress 2026

India must be part of AI safety regulation talks, says IndiaAI Mission COO

Large models aren't the answer to every enterprise AI problem: Articul8 CEO

OpenAI shares summaries of math problems solved by its unreleased model

Analysts have also recently trimmed their forecasts due to the sharp appreciation of the South Korean currency, which reduces the value of dollar-denominated overseas sales when converted into local currency.   "The market's focus has shifted to whether the sharp earnings growth that started a year ago would be sustainable," market analyst Kim Seok-hwan at Mirae Asset Securities said.

Analysts expect profit in the fourth quarter to grow 8.2% from the previous quarter, slowing from 20% sequential quarterly growth in the third quarter, with chip price growth abating.   Market research firm TrendForce expects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter from the preceding quarter, much slower than a second-quarter surge of roughly 60%.   The moderation in memory prices is being closely watched by investors after a more than year-long rally that propelled profit margins to record highs for the world's largest memory producers Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.   Third-quarter revenue would likely rise 127% to 195 trillion won from a year earlier, Samsung said.

The company will release detailed results, including a breakdown of earnings by business division, on October 29.   BIGGER-THAN-EXPECTED MOBILE LOSS   Memory chips are expected to account for the bulk of the earnings improvement.   Prices have soared due to the tight supply of conventional DRAM and NAND chips as well as growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), essential for processing vast amounts of data for AI applications.   Douglas Kim of Douglas Research Advisory estimated that Samsung's HBM bit shipments expanded by close to 50% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter, with Samsung trying to narrow the gap with SK Hynix in the HBM market.   But the memory chip boom presents a challenge for Samsung's other businesses, particularly its smartphone and consumer electronics divisions, which face mounting pressure from higher component costs.

Samsung's mobile business posted a larger-than-expected loss of more than $1 billion in the third quarter, analysts said.   Meanwhile, Samsung's contract chipmaking, or foundry, business is expected to remain loss-making because of the burden of fixed costs and still-low utilisation rates, analysts said.   However, utilisation is expected to improve over the next several quarters, supported by stronger demand for advanced manufacturing processes. Samsung has been seeking to narrow the gap with industry leader TSMC in advanced contract chip manufacturing.   Investors said they would also be closely watching for details of Samsung's shareholder return policy during its earnings call later this month.   More From This Section
